title: Thyroid gland anatomy: follicles, vessels and nerves
description: A butterfly gland of follicles that sets the body's metabolic rate.

questions.question: Where is the thyroid gland located?
questions.answer: The thyroid has two lateral lobes joined by an isthmus in the front of the neck, close to the larynx and upper trachea.

questions.question: What do thyroid follicles make?
questions.answer: Follicular cells use iodine and stored thyroglobulin in colloid to produce thyroid hormones. Nearby parafollicular cells produce calcitonin.

questions.question: What is the isthmus?
questions.answer: The bridge crossing the 2nd–4th tracheal rings, joining the two lobes. Function: Connects the lobes into a single gland.

questions.question: Where is the trachea & larynx located?
questions.answer: The gland wraps the airway; the cricoid cartilage and thyroid cartilage lie above. Function: Anatomical landmark and the reason goitres cause compressive symptoms.

questions.question: What is the function of the follicle & colloid?
questions.answer: Function: Synthesis and storage of thyroid hormone — the only endocrine gland that stores its product extracellularly. Spheres of follicular cells enclosing colloid (iodinated thyroglobulin). TSH stimulates iodide trapping, organification, coupling, and endocytosis of colloid to release T3/T4.
